about: Draft scripts for the sealed Lore book chapters II-X. Chapter I lives in source/src/lore-chapters.ts. Each chapter is six comic panels read left-to-right, top-to-bottom. caption, dialogue and scene follow LORE_CHAPTER_ONE; art is the panel brief used in that chapter's .prompt.txt. Only original characters appear in the artwork; champions from other universes are shown as glowing card frames or silhouettes, never drawn.

cast.rick: Rick Gramps, a sturdy elderly man with swept-back silver hair, short white beard, bushy brows, round brass goggles pushed up on his forehead, weathered olive long coat, wine-red scarf, fingerless gloves, one small brass cuff on his left wrist. Wry and determined, never a caricature.
cast.archivist: The Archivist, a young woman in an oversized midnight-blue hooded coat, short copper hair, carrying a small ring of gold keys. Calm and knowing.
cast.dealer: The Dealer, a towering faceless figure in a long coat made of overlapping playing-card backs, with enormous luminous pale hands and no visible face beneath a deep hood; violet light leaks from the gaps between its cards.

panels.caption: Every victory left something warm in his pocket.
panels.scene: Rick turns a newly won card over in his hand. A tiny sun rises inside its frame.
panels.art: close-up of Rick's gloved hand holding an ornate card; inside the card frame a miniature landscape glows as a tiny sun rises over it, light spilling onto his face

panels.scene: Rick holds the card to his ear. Faint wind and birdsong come from inside.
panels.art: Rick in a cluttered workshop of brass instruments holds the card to his ear with eyes narrowed, faint swirls of wind and tiny birds escape the card's edge

panels.caption: The Archivist kept count.
panels.dialogue: One key for every lock. One lock for every world.
panels.scene: The Archivist spreads her ring of gold keys across a table. Each key is cut differently.
panels.art: the Archivist sits across a worn wooden table and fans out a ring of many unique gold keys under a hanging lamp, Rick leans in, the keys cast long shadows

panels.dialogue: You turned one when you won.
panels.scene: A single key glows and turns by itself. A distant lock clicks open.
panels.art: one gold key on the table glows and rotates by itself; in the background through a round window a far-off floating card's golden lock thread snaps loose

panels.caption: One key had no teeth at all.
panels.dialogue: Then what does that one open?
panels.scene: Rick points at a smooth, blank key. The Archivist closes her hand around it.
panels.art: Rick points at a smooth blank key without teeth; the Archivist closes her hand over it protectively, her expression guarded for the first time

panels.caption: She did not answer. Somewhere, a deck was being cut.
panels.scene: The Archivist walks toward an arched doorway. Behind her, a shadow cuts a deck in two.
panels.art: the Archivist walks away down a vaulted corridor toward an arched doorway; on the far wall a huge shadow of two hands cuts a deck of cards, Rick watches from the foreground

panels.caption: The keys led down.
panels.scene: Rick and the Archivist descend a spiral staircase that winds around a shaft of floating pages.
panels.art: high angle view down a vast spiral staircase around a deep shaft filled with drifting parchment pages, Rick and the Archivist small on the steps, lantern light

panels.caption: A library of one book.
panels.scene: At the bottom stands a single enormous ledger, taller than a house, its pages turning on their own.
panels.art: an immense open ledger taller than a house on an ancient lectern in a dark round chamber, its pages turning by themselves, Rick tiny in front of it with goggles lowered

panels.caption: Every duel, written in gold.
panels.scene: The Archivist runs a finger down columns of gold ink. Fresh lines write themselves ahead of her.
panels.art: close-up of the Archivist's finger tracing columns of shimmering gold handwriting; further down the page new lines of gold are writing themselves as she watches

panels.scene: Rick finds his own name over and over, each entry struck through with a heavy black line.
panels.art: Rick leans close to the page, a magnifying lens over one goggle eye; the page shows rows of heavy black strike-through lines over glowing gold entries

panels.caption: He was not in the script.
panels.dialogue: Every time you win, the book has to change.
panels.scene: Black ink bleeds and rewrites a page as the Archivist watches, worried.
panels.art: the ledger page buckles as black ink bleeds across it and rewrites the gold lines; the Archivist steps back with worry, violet light rising from the paper

panels.scene: Rick tears out the page with his own name and pockets it, grinning.
panels.art: Rick tears a page out of the giant ledger with a defiant grin and stuffs it in his long coat; loose pages swirl upward around him like startled birds

panels.caption: The torn page summoned its author.
panels.scene: The card table shudders. Every card on it flips face down at once.
panels.art: the immense ancient card table from the empty-chair scene, every card on it flipping face down at once in a wave, candles guttering, Rick seated at the head

panels.caption: The Dealer.
panels.dialogue: You are sitting in my chair.
panels.scene: The Dealer rises from the far end of the table, its coat of card backs rustling.
panels.art: the Dealer rises at the far end of the long table, towering, faceless under its hood, coat of overlapping card backs, enormous pale luminous hands resting on the table edge

panels.dialogue: Retire. Forever. Every comfort. No more games.
panels.scene: The Dealer slides a single card across the table. It shows a quiet house by a lake.
panels.art: close-up of a giant pale hand sliding one card across the table toward Rick; the card shows a peaceful lakeside cottage at sunset, warm and tempting

panels.scene: The Archivist grips Rick's shoulder from behind.
panels.art: the Archivist stands behind Rick's chair, gripping his shoulder, her eyes fixed on the Dealer, her key ring clenched in her other hand

panels.scene: Rick flicks the card back. It spins through the air between them.
panels.art: Rick leans back and flicks the lakeside card back across the table with two fingers, the card spinning in mid-air, his expression unimpressed

panels.caption: The House does not lose. It only waits.
panels.scene: The Dealer's hands begin shuffling. Worlds blur past inside the cards.
panels.art: dramatic low angle of the Dealer's huge glowing hands shuffling a deck in a cascade; inside each blurred card a different tiny world flashes past, violet and gold light

panels.caption: The Dealer answered with a demonstration.
panels.scene: A giant hand closes around one floating card and starts to crumple it.
panels.art: a giant pale hand closes around one of the floating door-cards in the starry void and begins to crumple it, the tiny world inside darkening and tilting

panels.scene: The Archivist runs along a narrow bridge of light toward the crumpling card.
panels.art: the Archivist sprints along a narrow bridge of light across the void, hood flying back, reaching toward the crumpling card in the distance

panels.caption: Rick had one trick the Dealer didn't.
panels.scene: Rick throws his whole deck into the void. The cards lock edge to edge into a path.
panels.art: Rick hurls his entire deck into the void; the cards fly out and lock edge to edge into a glowing stepping-stone path leading toward the dying world

panels.scene: Rick snatches the half-crumpled card out of the Dealer's fingers.
panels.art: Rick leaps from the last card of the path and snatches the half-crumpled card out from between enormous glowing fingers, coat and scarf whipping behind him

panels.caption: Inside his collection, the world began to breathe again.
panels.scene: The card smooths flat in Rick's hand. Its little sun comes back on.
panels.art: close-up of the rescued card smoothing itself flat in Rick's palm, the tiny world inside relighting, a golden lock thread reattaching to his brass cuff

panels.caption: Collecting had never been a hobby. It was a rescue.
panels.dialogue: Then let's collect all of them.
panels.scene: Rick and the Archivist look out at thousands of locked worlds.
panels.art: Rick and the Archivist stand side by side on the card path, seen from behind, looking out at thousands of floating locked door-cards stretching to the horizon

panels.caption: The Ledger had one page she never let him read.
panels.scene: Rick returns alone to the Ledger and opens it to a page sealed with gold wax.
panels.art: Rick alone in the round ledger chamber breaks a gold wax seal on a page of the giant ledger, lantern light, furtive

panels.caption: The first entry. The first lock.
panels.scene: Pressed between the pages is a card showing the Archivist's face.
panels.art: pressed flat between huge ledger pages lies an old card bearing a portrait of the copper-haired Archivist, a heavy golden lock thread wrapped around it

panels.dialogue: I'm not from between the worlds. I'm a world.
panels.scene: The Archivist stands in the doorway. Her edges flicker like the border of a card.
panels.art: the Archivist stands in the arched doorway, her silhouette edged with a faint glowing rectangular card border, her expression sad and honest

panels.caption: Each key was a piece of home.
panels.dialogue: I've been unlocking everyone else first.
panels.scene: She holds up her key ring. Every key holds a tiny image of the same city.
panels.art: close-up of the key ring held up to the light; each gold key bow contains a tiny painted image of the same seaside city at different times of day

panels.dialogue: That's a terrible plan. I love it.
panels.scene: Rick laughs and hands the card back to her.
panels.art: Rick laughs warmly and offers the Archivist's card back to her with an open hand, she hesitates with the beginning of a smile

panels.caption: The blank key still had nowhere to go.
panels.scene: Rick glances at the toothless key on her ring, then at the cuff on his own wrist.
panels.art: a quiet two-shot: Rick's gaze moves from the smooth blank key on the Archivist's ring down to the small brass cuff on his own left wrist, which glints

panels.caption: The House changed the rules.
panels.scene: Ink-black copies of Rick's cards rise out of the arena floor.
panels.art: in the circular duel arena, figures made of dripping black ink rise up from the cracked floor shaped like card frames, faceless and hollow, violet light behind

panels.scene: Rick studies a counterfeit card. Its picture is a smear.
panels.art: Rick holds up an ink-black counterfeit card next to a genuine glowing one; the counterfeit's image is a blank smear, the genuine card shines

panels.caption: But his champions remembered who had freed them.
panels.scene: Rick's cards rise around him as glowing silhouettes, each a different shape.
panels.art: Rick's collected cards rise into the air around him and become tall glowing silhouettes of many different shapes and sizes, no faces or details visible, only light

panels.dialogue: Fakes left. Real ones, with me.
panels.scene: The Archivist points. The silhouettes surge forward.
panels.art: the Archivist points across the arena and the glowing silhouettes surge forward as a wave of gold light toward the ink figures

panels.caption: Ink cannot hold a shape it never earned.
panels.scene: The counterfeits splash apart into puddles.
panels.art: the black ink figures burst apart into splashes and puddles as gold light hits them, droplets frozen mid-air, dramatic action

panels.scene: Rick looks up at the Dealer's hand above the arena.
panels.art: low angle: Rick stands amid the ink puddles and looks straight up at the enormous pale hand hovering above the arena, which slowly curls into a fist

panels.caption: Almost every door stood open.
panels.scene: Hundreds of floating cards hang unlocked, their worlds bright.
panels.art: the starry void filled with hundreds of floating door-cards, their golden lock threads broken and drifting, each little world bright and alive

panels.caption: One card had been hidden in plain sight.
panels.scene: The Archivist points at a small dark card that drifts close behind Rick.
panels.art: the Archivist points past Rick's shoulder at a small dim card drifting just behind him like a shadow, wrapped in the heaviest lock thread of all

panels.dialogue: That's my home. It was destroyed.
panels.scene: Inside the card is a quiet street and a small house Rick recognises.
panels.art: close-up of the dim card: inside it a quiet suburban street at dusk and a small house with a porch light on, faded colours like an old photograph, Rick's face reflected in it

panels.caption: Not destroyed. Locked.
panels.dialogue: The first world the House ever took.
panels.scene: The Archivist holds up the toothless key. It matches the cuff on Rick's wrist.
panels.art: the Archivist holds the smooth blank key beside Rick's left wrist; the brass cuff on his wrist glows with exactly the same engraving pattern as the key's bow

panels.caption: He had worn the last key for four thousand years.
panels.scene: Rick unclasps the brass cuff. It unfolds into a key with teeth.
panels.art: Rick's gloved fingers unclasp the small brass cuff, which unfolds into an ornate brass key with intricate teeth, light pouring from its seams

panels.dialogue: Not yet. First I beat the House.
panels.scene: Rick closes his hand around the key and turns toward the table.
panels.art: Rick closes his fist around the brass key, jaw set, turning away from the dim home card toward the distant card table glowing on the horizon, the Archivist beside him

panels.caption: One game. Every world at stake.
panels.scene: Rick and the Dealer face each other across the ancient table.
panels.art: wide symmetrical shot down the length of the ancient card table: Rick seated at one end, the towering Dealer at the other, candles in a line between them, worlds floating overhead

panels.scene: The Dealer lays down card after card, each a locked world turned against Rick.
panels.art: the Dealer's enormous hands slam down a row of cards with heavy black lock chains; storms and fire erupt from them across the table toward Rick

panels.caption: Rick's hand was smaller. It was also loyal.
panels.scene: Rick's cards rise as glowing silhouettes and hold the line.
panels.art: Rick's cards rise in front of him as a wall of glowing silhouettes of many shapes, holding back the storm and fire, Rick calm behind them with one card raised

panels.scene: The Archivist throws her key ring across the table. Every key flies to its lock.
panels.art: the Archivist hurls her ring of gold keys over the table; the keys scatter through the air like comets, each streaking toward one of the Dealer's chained cards

panels.caption: Every chain broke at once.
panels.scene: The Dealer's cards turn bright and change sides.
panels.art: the black chains on the Dealer's cards shatter into gold sparks all at once; the cards turn bright and drift across the table to Rick's side, the Dealer recoiling

panels.dialogue: Check the ledger. You're the one crossed out.
panels.scene: Rick lays down his final card. The Dealer's coat starts coming apart into loose cards.
panels.art: Rick lays down one final card with a decisive snap; across the table the Dealer's coat of card backs begins to come apart, loose cards peeling away into the air

panels.caption: The House came apart one card at a time.
panels.scene: Under the Dealer's falling cards is a tired old man with a brass cuff.
panels.art: the Dealer's card-back coat falls away in a blizzard of cards, revealing beneath the hood a very old, tired, thin man with a white beard and an identical brass cuff on his wrist

panels.dialogue: I stopped playing. So I became the House.
panels.scene: The old man sits at the table. He looks like Rick, many centuries further on.
panels.art: the ancient tired man sits slumped at the table in the candlelight, his face a much older echo of Rick's; Rick stands opposite, stunned

panels.scene: Rick slides a single card across to his older self.
panels.art: Rick slides a single glowing card across the table to his older self, his expression softened, the old man's trembling hand reaching for it

panels.caption: One door left.
panels.scene: Rick turns the brass key in the lock of his home card. Light pours out.
panels.art: Rick turns the ornate brass key in a small golden lock on the dim home card; warm light floods out of the card across his face, the Archivist watching with her hand on her heart

panels.caption: Every world was free to leave. Most of them came back to play.
panels.scene: The arena fills with glowing visitors arriving through open card-doors.
panels.art: the circular duel arena at dawn filled with crowds of glowing silhouettes arriving through hundreds of open card-shaped doorways floating around the rim, banners of light, celebration

panels.caption: The chair at the head of the table stays empty now.
panels.scene: Rick hands the deck to the Archivist. The chair behind them stays empty.
panels.art: Rick hands an ornate deck to the smiling Archivist across the card table; behind them the great chair at the head of the table stands empty in a shaft of golden light
